text.p: International Business Machines Corp. Tuesday reported better-than-expected earnings of $3.93 a share the fourth quarter, compared with $3.09 a share for the 1995 quarter.

The world's largest computer maker said net income was $2.0 billion vs. $1.7 billion in the year-ago period. Wall Street analysts had expected earnings of $3.88 a share, on average, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates.
Revenues rose 6 percent to $23.1 billion, the company said.

The Armonk, N.Y.-based computer maker said growth in the quarter was good despite continued weakness in Europe. It also said that services revenues jumped 22 percent in the fourth quarter, personal computer sales rose but sales of mainframes fell.
In a break with tradition, IBM released its results after the stock market closed rather than before the market opened.
